Both are handled in a single fused pass over (z, y) rows so that each output\n// element is written exactly once, there is no second sweep over the grid, and the\n// work is distributed across threads in contiguous, cache-friendly chunks.\nvoid stencilIteration(const std::vector<Real>& input,\n                      std::vector<Real>& output,\n                      const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz) {\n    if (nx == 0 || ny == 0 || nz == 0) return;\n\n    const Real* __restrict in = input.data();\n    Real* __restrict out = output.data();\n    const size_t plane = nx * ny;\n    const bool hasInterior = (nx >= 3 && ny >= 3 && nz >= 3);\n\n#pragma omp parallel for collapse(2) schedule(static)\n    for (size_t z = 0; z < nz; ++z) {\n        for (size_t y = 0; y < ny; ++y) {\n            const size_t rowBase = z * plane + y * nx;\n            const Real* __restrict inRow = in + rowBase;\n            Real* __restrict outRow = out + rowBase;\n\n            const bool boundaryRow = !hasInterior ||\n                                     z == 0 || z == nz - 1 ||\n                                     y == 0 || y == ny - 1;\n            if (boundaryRow) {\n                // Entire row lies on the boundary: straight copy.\n                std::memcpy(outRow, inRow, nx * sizeof(Real));\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // x-boundary points of this row.\n            outRow[0] = inRow[0];\n            outRow[nx - 1] = inRow[nx - 1];\n\n            const Real* __restrict front  = inRow - nx;      // y-1\n            const Real* __restrict back   = inRow + nx;      // y+1\n            const Real* __restrict bottom = inRow - plane;   // z-1\n            const Real* __restrict top    = inRow + plane; Discard those pages so the\n// following parallel write re-faults them on the node of the thread that will use them.\n// The buffer reads as all-zero both before and after this call, so semantics are kept.\nvoid releasePagesForFirstTouch(std::vector<Real>& grid) {\n#ifdef __linux__\n    if (grid.empty()) return;\n    const long pageSize = sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE);\n    if (pageSize <= 0) return;\n    const uintptr_t pg = static_cast<uintptr_t>(pageSize);\n    const uintptr_t begin = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(grid.data());\n    const uintptr_t end = begin + grid.size() * sizeof(Real);\n    const uintptr_t alignedBegin = (begin + pg - 1) & ~(pg - 1);\n    const uintptr_t alignedEnd = end & ~(pg - 1);\n    if (alignedEnd > alignedBegin) {\n        madvise(reinterpret_cast<void*>(alignedBegin), alignedEnd - alignedBegin, MADV_DONTNEED);\n    }\n#else\n    (void)grid;\n#endif\n}\n\n// Parallel first-touch of a grid. The (z, y) row partition and static schedule are\n// identical to the ones used by stencilIteration, so every thread initialises exactly\n// the rows it will later compute on, keeping pages NUMA-local and warm in cache.\ntemplate <typename RowFn>\ninline void forEachRowParallel(const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz, RowFn&& rowFn) {\n    const size_t plane = nx * ny;\n#pragma omp parallel for collapse(2) schedule(static)\n    for (size_t z = 0; z < nz; ++z) {\n        for (size_t y = 0; y < ny; ++y) {\n            rowFn(z, y, z * plane + y * nx);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nvoid initializeGrid(std::vector<Real>& grid, const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz) {\n    releasePagesForFirstTouch(grid);\n    Real* __restrict g = grid.data();\n    forEachRowParallel(nx, ny, nz, [=](size_t, size_t, const size_t rowBase) {\n        for (size_t x = 0; x < nx; ++x) {\n            const size_t idx = rowBase + x;\n            g[idx] = (idx % 19) * 1.0;\n        }\n    });\n}\n\n// First-touch the scratch grid with the same thread/row mapping (contents stay zero).\nvoid touchGrid(std::vector<Real>& grid, const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz) {\n    releasePagesForFirstTouch(grid);\n    Real* __restrict g = grid.data();\n    forEachRowParallel(nx, ny, nz, [=](size_t, size_t, const size_t rowBase) {\n        std::memset(g + rowBase, 0, nx * sizeof(Real));\n    });\n}\n\n'''\nsrc = src.replace(old_init, new_init)\n\n# stencil: use the shared row iterator for identical partitioning\nold_st = src[src.index('void stencilIteration'):src.index('bool validateResult')]\nnew_st = '''void stencilIteration(const std::vector<Real>& input,\n                      std::vector<Real>& output,\n                      const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz) {\n    if (nx == 0 || ny == 0 || nz == 0) return;\n\n    const Real* __restrict in = input.data();\n    Real* __restrict out = output.data();\n    const size_t plane = nx * ny;\n    const bool hasInterior = (nx >= 3 && ny >= 3 && nz >= 3);\n\n    forEachRowParallel(nx, ny, nz, [=](const size_t z, const size_t y, const size_t rowBase) {\n        const Real* __restrict inRow = in + rowBase;\n        Real* __restrict outRow = out + rowBase;\n\n        const bool boundaryRow = !hasInterior ||\n                                 z == 0 || z == nz - 1 ||\n                                 y == 0 || y == ny - 1;\n        if (boundaryRow) {\n            // Entire row lies on the boundary: straight copy.\n            std::memcpy(outRow, inRow, nx * sizeof(Real));\n            return;\n        }\n\n        // x-boundary points of this row.\n        outRow[0] = inRow[0];\n        outRow[nx - 1] = inRow[nx - 1];\n\n        const Real* __restrict front  = inRow - nx;      // y-1\n        const Real* __restrict back   = inRow + nx;      // y+1\n        const Real* __restrict bottom = inRow - plane;   // z-1\n        const Real* __restrict top    = inRow + plane;   // z+1\n\n        // Interior: contiguous in x, vectorizes cleanly.\n#pragma omp simd\n        for (size_t x = 1; x < nx - 1; ++x) {\n            const Real center = inRow[x];\n            const Real left   = inRow[x - 1];\n            const Real right  = inRow[x + 1];\n            outRow[x] = (center + left + right + front[x] + back[x] + bottom[x] + top[x]) / 7.0;\n        }\n    });\n}\n\n'''\nsrc = src.replace(old_st, new_st)\n\nsrc = src.replace('''    initializeGrid(grid1, nx, ny, nz);\n''', '''    initializeGrid(grid1, nx, ny, nz);\n    touchGrid(grid2, nx, ny, nz);\n''')\nopen(p,'w').write(src)\nEOF\ngrep -n \"cstdint\" stencil3d/stencil3d.cpp || sed -i 's/#include <cstdlib>/#include <cstdint>\\n#include <cstdlib>/' stencil3d/stencil3d.cpp\ncmake --build /tmp/bld 2>&1 | grep -Ei \"warning|error\"; echo build-done\nB=/tmp/bld/stencil3d\n$B -r -v | grep -E \"Hash|Sum|Computation|Value range\"\n$B -x 64 -y 33 -z 17 -i 7 -r | grep -E \"Hash|Sum\"\nfor s in 1 2 3; do echo \"n=$s: $($B -x $s -i 3 -r | grep Hash) | base: $(/tmp/base/stencil3d -x $s -i 3 -r | grep Hash)\"; done\nfor t in 1 32 64 128 256; do best=0; for r in 1 2 3; do p=$(OMP_NUM_THREADS=$t OMP_PROC_BIND=close OMP_PLACES=cores $B -x 384 -i 10 | grep Performance | awk '{print $2}'); best=$(echo \"$p $best\" | awk '{print ($1>$2)?$1:$2}'); done; echo \"bound threads=$t best=$best MCUPS\"; done","description":"Apply NUMA-aware first-touch, rebuild, verify hashes, re-measure scaling","timeout":400000},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3280,"cache_read_input_tokens":29365,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3280},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7a2289c9-d06c-4f54-9414-ef5fddd936bb","uuid":"f1d46435-2546-42f1-b191-91a8b9bfc150","timestamp":"2026-10-16T19:51:23.091Z","request_id":"req_011Cg6VoNykZxMBRx56pJDPy"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011Cg6W1BbDzbXcFHUaoTkVt","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Done. The stencil3d benchmark now runs unconditionally with OpenMP, produces bit-identical results to the original, and runs about 20x faster than the serial baseline on this 2-socket, 128-core EPYC machine.\n\n**What changed in `stencil3d/stencil3d.cpp`**\n\n- **Fused stencil pass.** The interior stencil and the boundary copy are now one parallel sweep over (z, y) rows, with `collapse(2)` and static scheduling. Boundary rows are copied whole, interior rows copy their two x-edge cells and vectorize the rest with `omp simd`. Each output cell is written exactly once, which removes the original's full second pass over the grid. The expression and division by 7.0 are unchanged, so results match bit for bit.\n- **NUMA-aware first touch.** The vector constructor zero-fills both grids from the main thread, which puts every page on one NUMA node and roughly halved throughput in my tests. Both grids now have those pages released with `madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)` and re-touched in parallel using the exact same row partition as the stencil. Contents read as zero before and after, so semantics are preserved.\n- **Default thread pinning.** Unpinned threads migrated across sockets and ran up to 7x slower than pinned ones on this shared machine. The program now pins thread t to the t-th CPU of its affinity mask, but only when none of OMP_PROC_BIND, OMP_PLACES, GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY, or KMP_AFFINITY is set, so user settings always win.\n- **Parallel validation.** The NaN/Inf check and the min/max scan use OpenMP reductions.\n- The thread count is printed at startup. The Linux-specific pieces are guarded by `#ifdef __linux__` and degrade to no-ops elsewhere.\n\n**CMakeLists.txt** uses `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and links `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`. Executable name is unchanged, no new files or dependencies.\n\n**Verification.** Sum and FNV hash from the `-r` output match the original binary on the default 128³ grid and on 200x150x100, 5x300x7, 3x3x3, 1x50x50, and iteration counts 0, 1, 2, 4, 7, 11. The stencil3d benchmark now runs unconditionally with OpenMP, produces bit-identical results to the original, and runs about 20x faster than the serial baseline on this 2-socket, 128-core EPYC machine.\n\n**What changed in `stencil3d/stencil3d.cpp`**\n\n- **Fused stencil pass.** The interior stencil and the boundary copy are now one parallel sweep over (z, y) rows, with `collapse(2)` and static scheduling. Boundary rows are copied whole, interior rows copy their two x-edge cells and vectorize the rest with `omp simd`. Each output cell is written exactly once, which removes the original's full second pass over the grid. The expression and division by 7.0 are unchanged, so results match bit for bit.\n- **NUMA-aware first touch.** The vector constructor zero-fills both grids from the main thread, which puts every page on one NUMA node and roughly halved throughput in my tests. Both grids now have those pages released with `madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)` and re-touched in parallel using the exact same row partition as the stencil. Contents read as zero before and after, so semantics are preserved.\n- **Default thread pinning.** Unpinned threads migrated across sockets and ran up to 7x slower than pinned ones on this shared machine. The program now pins thread t to the t-th CPU of its affinity mask, but only when none of OMP_PROC_BIND, OMP_PLACES, GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY, or KMP_AFFINITY is set, so user settings always win.\n- **Parallel validation.** The NaN/Inf check and the min/max scan use OpenMP reductions.\n- The thread count is printed at startup. The Linux-specific pieces are guarded by `#ifdef __linux__` and degrade to no-ops elsewhere.\n\n**CMakeLists.txt** uses `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and links `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`. Executable name is unchanged, no new files or dependencies.\n\n**Verification.** Sum and FNV hash from the `-r` output match the original binary on the default 128³ grid and on 200x150x100, 5x300x7, 3x3x3, 1x50x50, and iteration counts 0, 1, 2, 4, 7, 11.
